html:
Bayezid I was sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1389 to 1402, called Yıldırım, "the Thunderbolt", for the speed of his campaigns. He nearly took Constantinople, but his empire collapsed when Timur defeated and captured him.

He came to the throne on the battlefield of Kosovo in 1389, where his father Murad I was killed. He had his brother put to death at once, the first known case of the Ottoman custom of royal fratricide. He then moved fast on two fronts:

  • In the Balkans he made Serbia a vassal and annexed Bulgaria in 1393.
  • In Anatolia he swallowed most of the Turkish emirates.
  • From 1394 he held Constantinople under blockade, building the fortress of Anadoluhisarı on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus. His great-grandson Mehmed II later built Rumelihisarı facing it.
  • In 1396 he crushed a large crusading army from Hungary, France and other lands at Nicopolis on the Danube.

The emperor Manuel II toured Europe seeking help, but rescue came from the east. The Anatolian rulers Bayezid had driven out turned to Timur, who crushed the Ottoman army at the Battle of Ankara in 1402 and took Bayezid prisoner. He died in captivity in 1403. His sons fought each other for eleven years before the state was reunited, and Constantinople gained half a century of life.
sum: Bayezid I was sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1389 to 1402, called Yıldırım, "the Thunderbolt", for the speed of his campaigns. He nearly took Constantinople, but his empire collapsed when Timur defeated and captured him.
